Abnormal Procedure

24 cards
Q1MEMORY ITEMS
In case of windshear encounter after V1, pilot pitch target should be:
SRS orders
Q2MEMORY ITEMS
During TCAS RA warning, if following the RA order would result in crossing the intruder altitude, what shall be the crew's action?
Always follow RA order, even if this results in crossing the intruder altitude, because these orders ensure the best altitude separation.
Q3MEMORY ITEMS
The correct standard callout when encountering a reactive windshear is:
WINDSHEAR TOGA
Q4MEMORY ITEMS
GPWS Caution "Too Low Gear - Too Low Flaps": a Go Around must be:
Performed
Q5MEMORY ITEMS
In case of windshear encounter after V1, should the FD bars not be displayed, pilot pitch target should be:
17.5 degrees
Q6MEMORY ITEMS
The aircraft is equipped with AP/FD TCAS. When a TCAS Traffic Advisory is triggered, what should be the flight crew action?
TCAS mode CHECK ARMED
Q7MEMORY ITEMS
The aircraft is not equipped with AP/FD TCAS mode. If a CLIMB RA is triggered during approach in CONF 3 or FULL, what shall the flight crew do?
GO-AROUND: perform and follow the SRS GA mode; monitor VERTICAL SPEED by checking that it remains out of the red area of the vertical speed scale, and take over if necessary.
Q8MEMORY ITEMS
What is true during the execution of the TAWS WARNING memory item?
Do not change configuration (Slats/Flaps, Gear) until clear of obstacle.
Q9MEMORY ITEMS
The correct pitch target when encountering a warning "TERRAIN AHEAD PULL UP" is:
FULL BACKSTICK
Q10MEMORY ITEMS
During Stall Recovery, in the case of lack of pitch down authority, the flight crew may:
Reduce thrust
Q11MEMORY ITEMS
The correct standard callout when encountering a warning "TERRAIN AHEAD PULL UP" is:
PULL UP TOGA
Q12ABN PROCEDURES
If smoke/fumes initially come out of the cockpit's ventilation outlets, or if smoke/fumes are detected in the cabin, what source of smoke may the crew suspect?
Air Conditioning Smoke
Q13ABN PROCEDURES
What are the objectives of the Immediate Actions in the [QRH] SMOKE/FUMES/AVNCS SMOKE procedure?
Flight crew protection; avoid any further contamination of the cockpit/cabin; communication with the cabin crew.
Q14ABN PROCEDURES
If smoke or fumes are detected by the crew, without any ECAM alert, what should the flight crew refer to?
The flight crew will refer directly to the [QRH] SMOKE/FUMES/AVNCS SMOKE procedure.
Q15ABN PROCEDURES
If the AVIONICS SMOKE ECAM alert is activated, but smoke or fumes are not perceptible, what should be the crew's consideration?
Consider a spurious alert and therefore stop the AVIONICS SMOKE procedure.
Q16ABN PROCEDURES
According to FCTM, when may the "Boxed items" in the [QRH] SMOKE/FUMES/AVNCS SMOKE procedure be applied?
They may be applied at any time, but not before the immediate actions.
Q17ABN PROCEDURES
If smoke/fumes initially come out of the cockpit's ventilation outlets, or if smoke/fumes are detected in the cabin, the crew may suspect an AIR COND SMOKE/FUMES. What can the crew expect shortly thereafter?
Several SMOKE alerts (cargo, lavatory, avionics) will be triggered.
Q18ABN PROCEDURES
When encountering volcanic ash, how many degrees should the pilot perform to exit the volcanic ash clouds?
Perform a 180-degree turn to exit quickly, because volcanic ash clouds can extend for hundreds of miles.
Q19ABN PROCEDURES
When entering volcanic ash clouds, if both engines flame out and speed indications are lost, what procedure should be used to get the required pitch attitude for the optimum relight speed?
All Engines Failure Procedure
Q20ABN PROCEDURES
For a nose-low situation with high bank angle, what is the correct order of actions?
5, 3, 6, 2, 1, 4 — Recognize and confirm the situation; takeover and disconnect AP/A/THR; recover from stall if required; adjust roll in the shortest direction to wings level; adjust thrust and drag; recover level flight.
Q21ABN PROCEDURES
Regarding the [QRH] SMOKE/FUMES/AVNCS SMOKE procedure, how shall the crew perform the "Source identification and fighting" section?
According to the source they suspect, the crew will enter ONE of the 3 paragraphs.
Q22ABN PROCEDURES
Regarding the management of smoke/fumes in-flight, if the smoke/fumes source is not immediately identified and isolated, what must the flight crew do?
Initiate the diversion before entering the identification and isolation part of the procedure.
Q23ABN PROCEDURES
For a nose-high situation, what is the correct order of actions?
6, 3, 5, 1, 2, 4 — Recognize and confirm the situation; takeover and disconnect AP/A/THR; apply nose-down pitch order; adjust thrust; adjust roll not to exceed 60 degrees; recover level flight.
Q24ABN PROCEDURES
The [QRH] SMOKE/FUMES/AVNCS SMOKE procedure contains the "Immediate Actions" section. In what case shall this section be performed?
For all cases of smoke or fumes, whatever the source.
✦ Correct information only — synchronized with the study cards.

Pack operation is?

Spoilers 2, 3 and 4

TRUE

TRUE

Q1A320 Performance
TOGA is the maximum thrust certified for takeoff. In the case of one engine out, the TOGA thrust rating may be used for a maximum of _____.
10 minutes
Q2A320 Performance
FLEX takeoff is permitted on wet runways.
TRUE
Q3A320 Performance
FLEX takeoff is permitted on contaminated runways.
FALSE
Q4A320 Performance
The Go-Around Climb Gradient must be at least equal to:
2.10% and the gradient published in the airport chart
Q5A320 Performance
For a badly paved runway or when accelerate-stop distance is limited, what takeoff configuration is recommended?
CONF 2 or 3
Q6A320 Performance
On the A320, according to FCOM, what is the recommended takeoff configuration when the crew is expecting a high altitude takeoff?
CONF 2 or 3 to improve comfort
Q7A320 Performance
According to FCOM/Performance, what is Referenced Speed (VREF)?
VREF is equal to the VLS of CONF FULL, used to determine the final approach speed (VAPP) when a system failure affects the landing performance.
Q8A320 Performance
According to FCOM / QRH Severe Turbulence, what is true about CONF FULL when the crew flies the aircraft manually in turbulent conditions?
CONF FULL provides better handling capability in turbulent conditions.
Q9A320 Performance
What speed is a good approximation of the maximum endurance speed?
GREEN DOT SPD
Q10A320 Performance
TFLEX cannot be lower than:
OAT
Q11A320 Performance
CDL items may affect Takeoff Parameters.
TRUE
Q12A320 Performance
What does the Cost Index influence?
OPT ALT
Q13A320 Performance
TOGA is the maximum thrust certified for takeoff. When all engines are operative, the TOGA thrust rating must not be used more than _____.
5 minutes
Q14A320 Performance
What does the flight crew use to determine the landing performance level?
RCAM
Q15A320 Ops Specs
Currently for A320 Fleet, what EDTO operation is VietJet currently authorized?
Not available on A320 Fleet
Q16A320 Ops Specs
For A320 aircraft, registration VN-A658, what is the tailwind limitation for landing?
15 kt
Q17A320 Ops Specs
For A320 aircraft, registration VN-A658, what is the maximum demonstrated crosswind for takeoff and landing?
38 kt
Q18A320 Ops Specs
For A320 aircraft, registration VN-A658, what is the maximum tailwind for takeoff?
10 kt
Q19A320 Limitations
Maximum Tire Speed:
195 kt GS
Q20A320 Limitations
Maximum altitude for APU bleed operation is:
22,500 ft
Q21A320 Limitations
Use of APU Bleed Air for wing anti-ice is not permitted.
TRUE
Q22A320 Limitations
Wipers Maximum Speed:
230 kt
Q23A320 Limitations
During refuel/defuel procedures, if a fuel spill occurs:
Shutdown APU
Q24A320 Limitations
On A320/321 aircraft, the Maximum Positive Differential Pressure is:
9.0 PSI
Q25A320 Limitations
Maximum Runway Altitude:
9200 ft
Q26A320 Limitations
Flight Maneuvering Load Acceleration Limits - Clean Configuration:
-1 g to +2.5 g
Q27A320 Limitations
Minimum Cabin Altitude Selection:
-2000 FT
Q28A320 Limitations
APU Bleed Air is available at:
22500 FT
Q29A320 Limitations
Takeoff Thrust/TOGA with all engines operative is limited to:
5 min

A320 PERFORMANCE
Q1 · TOGA is the maximum thrust certified for takeoff. In the case of one engine out, the TOGA thrust rating may be used for a maximum of _____. — 10 minutes
Q2 · FLEX takeoff is permitted on wet runways..
Q3 · The source marks this statement as false: FLEX takeoff is permitted on contaminated runways..
Q4 · The Go-Around Climb Gradient must be at least equal to: — 2.10% and the gradient published in the airport chart
Q5 · For a badly paved runway or when accelerate-stop distance is limited, what takeoff configuration is recommended — CONF 2 or 3
Q6 · On the A320, according to FCOM, what is the recommended takeoff configuration when the crew is expecting a high altitude takeoff — CONF 2 or 3 to improve comfort
Q7 · According to FCOM/Performance, what is Referenced Speed (VREF) — VREF is equal to the VLS of CONF FULL, used to determine the final approach speed (VAPP) when a system failure affects the landing performance.
Q8 · According to FCOM / QRH Severe Turbulence, what is true about CONF FULL when the crew flies the aircraft manually in turbulent conditions — CONF FULL provides better handling capability in turbulent conditions.
Q9 · What speed is a good approximation of the maximum endurance speed — GREEN DOT SPD
Q10 · TFLEX cannot be lower than: — OAT
Q11 · CDL items may affect Takeoff Parameters..
Q12 · What does the Cost Index influence — OPT ALT
Q13 · TOGA is the maximum thrust certified for takeoff. When all engines are operative, the TOGA thrust rating must not be used more than _____. — 5 minutes
Q14 · What does the flight crew use to determine the landing performance level — RCAM
Q15 · Currently for A320 Fleet, what EDTO operation is VietJet currently authorized — Not available on A320 Fleet
Q16 · For A320 aircraft, registration VN-A658, what is the tailwind limitation for landing — 15 kt
Q17 · For A320 aircraft, registration VN-A658, what is the maximum demonstrated crosswind for takeoff and landing — 38 kt
Q18 · For A320 aircraft, registration VN-A658, what is the maximum tailwind for takeoff — 10 kt
Q19 · Maximum Tire Speed: — 195 kt GS
Q20 · Maximum altitude for APU bleed operation is: — 22,500 ft
Q21 · Use of APU Bleed Air for wing anti-ice is not permitted..
Q22 · Wipers Maximum Speed: — 230 kt
Q23 · During refuel/defuel procedures, if a fuel spill occurs: — Shutdown APU
Q24 · On A320/321 aircraft, the Maximum Positive Differential Pressure is: — 9.0 PSI
Q25 · Maximum Runway Altitude: — 9200 ft
Q26 · Flight Maneuvering Load Acceleration Limits - Clean Configuration: — -1 g to +2.5 g
Q27 · Minimum Cabin Altitude Selection: — -2000 FT
Q28 · APU Bleed Air is available at: — 22500 FT
Q29 · Takeoff Thrust/TOGA with all engines operative is limited to: — 5 min

Special Operations

44 cards
Q1LVO
Regarding LVO, what is the alert height on A320/321 aircraft?
100 ft
Q2LVO
For CAT II/III approaches, which RVR measurement is mandatory?
TDZ
Q3LVO
According to VJ OM-A, what is true regarding low visibility taxi?
All checklists, flight controls check and briefing shall be done when the aircraft is stopped with the parking brake ON.
Q4LVO
On A320 aircraft, during automatic rollout with one engine inoperative or one thrust reverser inoperative, when may the crew use the remaining thrust reverser?
Provided that no more than idle thrust is used, and the wind does not exceed the maximum wind conditions for automatic rollout.
Q5LVO
Using LOC G/S Guidance for a CAT II/III approach, under what conditions must the crew perform a go-around below 1,000 ft AGL?
When external visual references are not sufficient and there is an amber caution (single chime); and when external visual references are not sufficient and landing capability is downgraded below the approach category defined during the briefing.
Q6LVO
What landing category displayed on the FMA is a fail-operational automatic landing system?
CAT III DUAL
Q7LVO
Refer to OM-A 8.4.3: Single-Engine Taxi is allowed in Low-Visibility Operations.
FALSE
Q8LVO
During ILS approaches, above 200 ft RA, if the transmitter failure lasts longer than 7 seconds, what happens to the AP and FD?
The AP disengages and the FD reverts to its basic modes.
Q9LVO
During pre-flight preparations, if the weather forecast at the destination airport is below CAT I minima, the crew must verify that the weather forecast at alternate airports is at least equal to:
CAT I minima
Q10LVO
Flight crew may not continue approach below CAT II DH without what visual references?
At least 3 longitudinal lights of: Approach lights; or TDZ lights; or Runway centerline lights; or Runway edge lights; and at least 1 lateral element, like Approach light crossbar; or Runway threshold lights.
Q11LVO
On A320 aircraft, in case of one engine inoperative, CAT II and CAT III fail passive autoland are approved in which configuration?
Configuration FULL only
Q12LVO
Practice Autoland is permitted on all runways with a published CAT II/III approach regardless of location.
TRUE
Q13LVO
Which statement is correct?
For a fail-passive flight control system, the pilot assumes control of the aircraft after a failure.
Q14LVO
According to VJ OM-A, who can be PF during Low Visibility Takeoff?
CM1 must be PF
Q15LVO
According to VJ OM-A, LVO approaches with the CM2 as PF shall only be permitted in abnormal situations (e.g. incapacitation).
TRUE
Q16LVO
According to VJ OM-A, during a low visibility approach, if a pilot becomes incapacitated, what is the preferable action for the remaining pilot?
Divert to an alternate airport with better weather condition.
Q17LVO
According to VJ OM-A, Low Visibility Takeoff procedure is not applicable in stormy weather conditions.
TRUE
Q18LVO
According to VietJet OMA, Low Visibility Takeoff is a takeoff where the Runway Visual Range is less than:
400 m
Q19LVO
On A321 aircraft, in case of one engine inoperative, CAT II and CAT III fail passive autoland are approved in which configuration?
Both Configuration 3 and FULL are approved
Q20LVO
According to VietJet OMA, for a CAT II/III approach, the aircraft shall meet all stable approach criteria by 1,000 feet AAL, with no speed exceptions.
TRUE
Q21PBN
What is the difference between RNAV and RNP?
RNAV is navigation performance WITHOUT on-board performance monitoring & alerting; RNP is navigation performance WITH on-board performance monitoring & alerting.
Q22PBN
The FMS vertical profile does not take into account the effect of low OAT. What is true concerning the use of vertical managed guidance?
Vertical managed guidance must not be used when the actual OAT is below the minimum temperature indicated on the approach chart; and it may not be used when temperature corrections are required (FINAL APP mode may not be engaged).
Q23PBN
During RNP Approach with LNAV minima, if NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD is displayed on one ND:
Continue APPR using the appropriate remaining AP/FD
Q24PBN
When performing RNP approach with LNAV minima by using FINAL APP guidance, what is the crew action if the vertical guidance is not satisfactory?
Revert to NAV-FPA
Q25PBN
If RNP approach is expected, which NOTAM regarding the Technical Standard Order (TSO) is applicable for A320 FMS/GNSS?
TSO-C129
Q26PBN
For RNP Approach with LNAV and LNAV/VNAV minima, if a "TOO STEEP PATH" is displayed after the FDP:
Do not use FINAL APP mode
Q27PBN
What are the actions of the flight crew before entering PBN airspace?
Check that the required PBN equipment is operative; check Navigation Accuracy HIGH displayed on the MCDU PROG page.
Q28PBN
During RNAV 1 SID/STAR, what would be the RNAV 1 capability if one ND is lost?
RNAV 1 capability may be maintained, since the temporary display of ND information via the PFD/ND switch is permitted on PM side.
Q29PBN
RNP Approach with LNAV minima can be performed using FINAL APP guidance.
TRUE
Q30PBN
RNP Approach with LNAV minima can be performed using NAV FPA guidance.
TRUE
Q31PBN
When performing RNP approaches, the final approach course must be intercepted not later than ____ from the FAF.
2 nm
Q32PBN
During RNAV APPR with LNAV minima, if the vertical guidance is not satisfactory, the flight crew may:
Continue APPR using NAV-FPA
Q33PBN
The Final Descent Point is:
The waypoint from which starts the FMS segment with coded FPA
Q34PBN
RNP Approach with LNAV minima can be performed using TRK FPA guidance.
FALSE
Q35PBN
For Baro-VNAV (LNAV/VNAV minima), what is the maximum discrepancy between altimeters?
75 ft during final approach; 100 ft to be cross-checked before FAF.
Q36PBN
For an EARLY STABILIZED APPR, to ensure timely deceleration, the flight crew must:
Enter Vapp at the FDP
Q37PBN
If RNP approach is expected, can the crew use the aircraft's GPS RAIM PREDICTION TOOL on PROG PAGE during preflight planning?
No. This tool is not approved for use in preflight planning as it does not account for the loss of satellites.
Q38PBN
When performing RNP approaches, if GPS PRIMARY LOST on one ND, what would be the flight crew's action?
Use the appropriate remaining AP/FD
Q39PBN
During RNP Approach with LNAV minima, if GPS PRIMARY LOST is displayed on one ND:
Continue approach using the appropriate remaining AP/FD
Q40PBN
A new RAIM availability check is required if ETA is more than ____ minutes different from ETA used during pre-flight planning.
15 minutes
Q41PBN
RNP Approach with LNAV/VNAV minima can be performed using NAV FPA guidance.
FALSE
Q42PBN
When performing RNP approaches, if GPS PRIMARY LOST on both ND, what would be the flight crew's action?
Discontinue the approach if external visual references are not sufficient to proceed visually.
Q43PBN
During RNAV APPR with LNAV minima, if NAV ACCUR DOWNGRAD is displayed on both NDs:
Discontinue APPR if visual references are not sufficient to proceed visually
Q44PBN
When performing an RNAV APCH, direct-to clearance may be accepted to IAF provided that resulting track change at IAF does not exceed how many degrees?
45 degrees
✦ Correct information only — synchronized with the study cards.

Adverse Weather

173 cards
Q1New Question Group 1
In crosswind conditions, during rollout, the reversers have a destabilizing effect on the airflow around the rudder and thus decrease the efficiency of the rudder. What is the recommended technique in this case?
Pilot will consider to set reversers back to REV IDLE. Rudder and differential braking should be used to correct back to the runway centerline
Q2New Question Group 1
The ND indicates turbulence areas in magenta within:
40NM
Q3New Question Group 1
According to OM-A 8.3.8.2.2, if the braking action encountered is not as good as reported, the PIC shall:
Report the actual encountered braking action via AIREP
Q4New Question Group 1
‘According to FCTM, regarding operations in convective weather, the flight crew must assume that all convective clouds are dangerous, even if the weather return is weak
TRUE
Q5New Question Group 1
The basic plain magenta indication on the ND indicates
Potential severe turbulences
Q6New Question Group 1
With the presence of icing contaminants on the wing, the wing critical angle of attack is
Decrease
Q7New Question Group 1
According to FCOM - Performance, what is the description of Dry Snow?
Dry snow is snow that if compacted by hand, does not stay compressed when released. The wind can blow dry snow
Q8New Question Group 1
According to FCTM, during descent, adjust the tilt so as to:
Maintain the ground returns on top of the ND.
Q9New Question Group 1
In the case of UNEVEN contamination on a wet or contaminated runway, flight crew may consider which of the following?
DESELECT AUTOBRK
Q10New Question Group 1
Jet engines have a limit on the amount of water they can ingest
TRUE
Q11New Question Group 1
De-icing/Anti-icing fluid must be heated for use
TRUE
Q12New Question Group 1
When operating the weather rader in Manual mode, the GCS function is available,
FALSE
Q13New Question Group 1
For A320/A321, having performed engine ground ice shedding procedure, rolling takeoff can be
FALSE 1c)
Q14New Question Group 1
According to FCTM, the “area of greatest threat” must be avoided by at least:
20NM
Q15New Question Group 1
Engines and APU can either be stopped or running during de-icing/ant-icing,
TRUE
Q16New Question Group 1
Lowest Operational Use Temperature (LOUT) is
The lowest temperature at which the de-icing/anti-icing fluid properly flows off critical surfaces during takeoff while maintaining freezing point buffer
Q17New Question Group 1
According to OM-A 8.3.8.3.9, When flight crew receives information with aerodromes having TS, or +RA, or TSRA, the Captain must be:
PF
Q18New Question Group 1
Its the flight crew responsibility to follow limitations, notes and cautions specific to each de- fluid type and brand
TRUE
Q19New Question Group 1
Consider a MINIMUM distance of __NM from the convective clouds to make a decision of weather avoidance
40NM
Q20New Question Group 1
According to OM-A 8.3.8.2, during operations on adverse runway conditions, it may be necessary to apply performance corrections in the form of
Runway length increment; Reduction in allowable take-off/landing weight; Reduction in allowable crosswind component
Q21New Question Group 1
For A320/A321 CEO, the maximum time to next engine acceleration (without maintenance task to deice engines) is
The difference between 30 minutes AT at or below 3° and the taxiin time of the previous flight
Q22New Question Group 1
Regarding flaps/stats operation in icing conditions:
For departure, do not extend flaps/slats until reaching the holding point; For arrival, do not retract flaps/slats until visual inspection is performed post-flight
Q23New Question Group 1
According to OM-A, in the case of SHRA at the aerodrome, and if the aerodrome has no report of braking action, the maximum crosswind component must be:
15kts 1c)
Q24New Question Group 1
On ground with contaminated surfaces or de-icing fluid on radio altimeter antennas, the flight crew can disregard the erroneous alerts/callouts but must check that the radio altimeter values are indicated on the PFD before entering the runway
TRUE 1c)
Q25New Question Group 1
Clear ice can be
Difficult to detect during walk-arounds, especially in poor lighting or when the wing is wet; Formed on upper wing surface, often with frost on the underside, especially with sub-zero fuel and precipitation
Q26New Question Group 1
When the temperature is lower than ISA, the FPA that the aircraft actually flies is less steep than the FPA that the ADIRS computes?
TRUE
Q27New Question Group 1
For A320/A321 with CFM engines, engine ground shedding will be performed with the THR LEVERS set to
Minimum 70% N1 for 30s
Q28New Question Group 1
According to OM-A 8.3.8.3.8, if itis not possible to avoid flying through or near to a thunderstorm, the recommended penetration speed must be followed and:
Note the TRIM setting
Q29New Question Group 1
According to OM-A 8.3.8.3, All thunderstorms are:
Considered hazardous
Q30New Question Group 1
For A320/A321 fleet: on the underside of the wing tank areas, a maximum layer of 3 mm (0.125 in) of frost is acceptable
TRUE
Q31New Question Group 1
In the terminal area thunderstorms should be avoided, no less than:
3NM
Q32New Question Group 1
Ice crystals are dificult to detect with the weather radar due to their low reflectivity
TRUE
Q33New Question Group 1
According to OM-A 8.3.8.2.5, if rain, hail, sleet or snow showers have been encountered on the approach or have recently crossed the airport, the flight crew shall
Check with the runway state with ATC before commencing or continuing the approach
Q34New Question Group 1
For A320/A321 CEO, with freezing rain, freezing drizzle, freezing fog or heavy snow, the maximum, time to next engine acceleration (without maintenance task to deice engines) is
The difference between 10 minutes AT at or below 3°C) and the tax:-in time of the previous flight
Q35New Question Group 1
For A320/A321 fleet, i VENTS AVNCS SYS FAULT alert appears, the crew shall
Reset the AEVC circuit breaker (AIR COND/AVNCS/VENT/MONG Y17 on 122VU).
Q36New Question Group 1
According to OM-A 8.3.8.3.9, When flight crew receives information with aerodromes having TS, or +RA, or TSRA, the new VIS value will be:
Published minima + 300m 1c)
Q37New Question Group 1
Flight crew shall
Observe engine shedding procedures; Follow local airport communication procedures and phraseology (when available)
Q38New Question Group 1
Outside a thunderstorm, severe shears have been encountered thousands of feet above and _ laterally
20NM

The final decision whether to de-ice/anti-ice the aircraft rests with the PIC
TRUE

IFin contact with human skin, the de-cing/anti-icing can cause burn and skin iritation
TRUE

De-icing/Anti-icing fluid can be sprayed into the engines and APU
FALSE

According to FCTM, concerning vertical avoidance, the flight crew should avoid flying below a convective cloud:
TRUE

For two-step de-icing/anti-icing method, Holdover Time starts

According to OM-A 8.3.8.3.4, itis allowed to take-off and land in the face of an approaching thunderstorm
FALSE 1c)

The PWS function can operate with the weather radar set to OFF, provided that: - The PWS switch is in the AUTO position, and - Aircraft radio height below 2300ft (1800ft on some aircraft), and - At least one engine running, and - Aircraft ground speed greater than 3Okt
TRUE 1c)
Q46New Question Group 1
According to FCTM, regarding avoidance techniques, it is preferred to:
Deviate Laterally
Q47New Question Group 1
For A320/A321, APU BLEED can be switched on after completion of spraying operation by at least
5 minutes
Q48New Question Group 1
"Cold-soaked" wings occur when
The aircraft wings contain cold fuel which reduces wings' surface temperature to 0°C or (o} below, forming frost by freezing moisture on the wing and tank surfaces
Q49New Question Group 1
According to FOTM "Flare and Touchdown’, in crosswind conditions, at which point shall the pilot use the rudder to align the aircraft with the runway heading?
During the flare
Q50New Question Group 1
An aircraft scanning the weather sees that the storm cell is 80NM away. The flight crew uses a manual tit of 2 degrees down, and after a few seconds the weather image disappears. According to the formula provided in the FCTM, this indicates that the:
The top of the storm cell is 16000FT below
Q51New Question Group 1
For one-step de-icing/anti-icing method, Holdover Time starts
At the start of application
Q52New Question Group 1
Turning maneouvers while being subjected to turbulence increases:
Upsets; Aircraft stress loads
Q53New Question Group 1
In the event of a lightning strike, the flight crew shall
‘Check all radio communication and navigational equipment; ‘Check all four quadrantal headings of the magnetic compass after landing; Record the lighting strike in the ETLB
Q54New Question Group 1
According to FCTM, concerning lateral deviations, it is preferrable to deviate upwind of the weather instead of downwind. Why?
The upwind side usually has less turbulence and hail
Q55New Question Group 1
For de-icing/anti-icing, both wings can be treated unevenly
FALSE
Q56New Question Group 1
For A320/A321 with CFM engines, if the is freezing rain, freezing drizzle, freezing fog or heavy snow, engine ground shedding will be performed with the THR LEVERS set to
Minimum 70% N1 (NO HOLD TIME)
Q57New Question Group 1
The function of de-icing fluid is
Removing frozen contaminants from aircraft surfaces.
